subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal gateway SIGTERM/SIGINT cancel active managed exec children, preserve background/yielded exec sessions, or only add diagnostics while leaving current process preservation behavior intact?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves active runs on normal shutdown and preserves yielded/background exec sessions on abort; changing that can prevent dirty shutdowns but may terminate user work.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Make normal gateway stop reject new work, cancel foreground active managed exec runs before the watchdog, and document or separately handle any background/yielded exception.

options.title: Preserve background work and add visibility
options.body: Keep active/background exec preservation as the default and add diagnostics or operator visibility so shutdown blockers can be identified without killing work automatically.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this open behind #12554 until maintainers choose the broader session kill/list/process-group model.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Make normal gateway stop reject new work, cancel foreground active managed exec runs before the watchdog, and document or separately handle any background/yielded exception.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent process-supervisor and agent process refactors make this the best current routing candidate for the shutdown/process lifecycle policy choice.
